claims.hypothesis: Is the neutral gas around the ionized region in Y1 porous, enabling ionizing photon escape?
claims.experiment: Fit CLOUDY two-phase models to L[OIII], L[CII], L_UV, L_IR ratios
claims.finding: About 75% of the HII region surface is exposed to intercloud space

evidence.quote: indicating that $\approx75 \%$ of the ionized gas region is exposed to intercloud space

claims.hypothesis: Does the conclusion depend on fixed parameters?
claims.experiment: Varied SFH, age, metallicity, C/O, and Td
claims.result: All variants consistent within errors; cov_PDR=1 rejected in all

evidence.quote: Even in this case, the solution of $cov_\mathrm{PDR}=1$ is rejected

claims.finding: Comparable to local compact HII regions, so early evolutionary stage

evidence.quote: This size scale is as large as a compact H II region found in the Milky Way

why_this_method.value: Multi-phase modeling can break degeneracy between ionizing sources and gas conditions

evidence.quote: The key to resolving the degeneracy between ionizing sources and gas physical conditions lies in performing more detailed modeling of the ISM properties.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Density-bounded HII region omitted to reduce free parameters

evidence.quote: we omit the density-bounded H II region (cite: Beckman2000; Nakajima-Ouchi2014) in our model to decrease the number of free parameters.

limitations_admitted.value: Only three free parameters due to few observables; single-phase ionized gas cannot reproduce [O II]

evidence.quote: our modeling assumes a single-phase ionized gas component characterized by a single set of gas density and ionization parameter.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only 3 observables constrain 3 free parameters, so the fit is nearly saturated
Td and L_IR rely on a single continuum point
Inferred cov_PDR depends on assumed Td and metallicity
Magnification of integrated galaxy applied uniformly across components
